system.summary: Homophonic substitution of graphic signs and figures for French letters, with a numeric nomenclator of common words and names (12 il, 13 qui, 14 que, 35 parce que, 76 le roi de Navarre).
system.doubled_letters: special sign for some (yy = ss, T= = m/mm)
system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo's published partial tables for Mayenne-Forget Cipher-1; used as the starting key and corrected on the leaves.
system.notes: 87 entries in key.json, 42 of them code groups (19 marked unidentified '+', 4 names '*'). Several signs are confusable by shape (i/n/s, s/i, e/u at 0.91-0.93 correlation), so at the level of reading the cipher behaves as polyphonic and the language model chooses. A three-cipher hypothesis was made and retracted: all nine leaves tested answer to Cipher-1. Split on 14 Oct 2026 (one key per entry): Matignon's Cipher-3 leaves (fr. 15572 f. 276, fr. 15571 f. 179) are the entry matignon1586c3. f. 79r, once taken for a crib of 'Cipher-2', is Cipher-1 (the solved key reads it); the genuine Cipher-2 leaves fr. 15572 ff. 218-219 are not part of any entry (not attempted).

prior_solution.where: Tomokiyo, cryptiana: partial key tables for Cipher-1 and short openings of ff. 143, 150, 154 and 'f. 111'; contemporary decipherments of sibling leaves (f. 14v in f. 15r, f. 18 in f. 19, ff. 78-79 in the margin). Contemporary clear copies of ff. 143, 149v-150 and 154r-v bound as ff. 155-157 of the same volume, overlooked here until Michael Brackx found them (issue #70, 21 Oct 2026). No printed decipherment found (17 Sept 2026).

conditions.human_role: Project work: no target-specific intervention recorded. From 21 Oct 2026 the entry also carries Michael Brackx's contributed readings and key corrections (issues #64, #68-#71), reviewed and spot-checked here.
tools: line fitting and tiling (fitlines.py, rowcut.py, mtile.py)
character 6-gram French LM from Berger de Xivrey (mklm.py)
beam decoder over candidate-letter sets (solve.py, dec.py)

solution.what: Checked Tomokiyo's list: ff. 110, 123-124, 143, 150, 154, 173, 196, 201 undeciphered in Cipher-1, with partial tables and short openings; deciphered siblings ff. 14/15, 18-21/19, 78-79, 91-92. No printed decipherment found.
Mapped folios to Gallica canvases (double-page openings, drifting offset, two foliations).
Re-derived the Cipher-1 key from Tomokiyo's table, checked against the f. 14v/f. 15r crib and the f. 143 cipher; added values not in his table.
f. 143 recto, 21 lines, in three passes (three, five, eight tiles a line); uniform line grid found to corrupt the second half and replaced.
f. 143r decoded with the key and the LM beam decoder: about two thirds read, agreeing with Tomokiyo's opening and running past it.
Word-aware decoder (wdec.py) tried against the character decoder on f. 143: no gain; residue is transcription.
ff. 196 and 201 identified as one despatch enciphered twice, with clear head and foot cribs.
f. 18 cipher / f. 19 clear decipherment pair found and verified (14 = que, 52 = plustost); labelled glyph exemplars mined from it.
Confusable figures measured at 0.91-0.93 correlation: not separable by shape, reading is polyphonic.
readleaf.py (segment, match exemplars, beam-decode) recovers about 70% of plaintext characters on the crib leaf; exemplars do not transfer to f. 143's hand.
Figure-unit arithmetic proposed code 82 = le Prince de Conde; later retracted (line 8 'z' was the page edge).
Those leaves decoded in stretches: pay crisis of April 1586, lenders refusing, siege report naming 'le mareschal de Matignon', Mayenne's plan for Gascony.
ff. 196 and 201 aligned: 57% identical figures, 8 runs of 8+; shuffled control 12%, no runs.
Claimed ff. 123-124 and f. 110 were two further ciphers, from figure-frequency profiles; a 'rouergue' pattern on f. 79r gave five values for 'Cipher-2'.
Solved key vs scrambled keys: ff. 123-124 -2.35 vs -2.50..-2.53 per figure; f. 110 +2.07 gap. Three-cipher claim and the f. 79r values retracted.
f. 78v margin decipherment: cribem.py seeded with the solved key reaches alignment 106 vs 3-41 for scrambles; the key recovers the margin text.
ff. 123-124 (4,278 figures) transcribed and decoded: f. 124r reads well, f. 124v in fragments, f. 123r badly.
f. 110: 1,699 figures transcribed at three and five columns; magnification not the limit.
f. 110: automated glyph segmentation and clustering (fails its control on f. 154), seeded solve (moves 23 of 27 labels off the key), cold solve (-2.27 per figure, no continuous French).

Coverage measured instead of estimated: measure.py decodes every transcription with key.json and the 6-gram model, counts a token read only if keyed and inside a >=3-word, >=10-letter lexical run, and runs a 3-seed scrambled-key control per leaf. Result 4,325/12,994 transcribed tokens (0.33), 0.28 of the whole target with untranscribed lines counted (0.22 chance-corrected); f. 110 scores at its scrambled floor. Also found: f. 196 has 31 cipher lines (26 transcribed), f. 177 has 29 (24 transcribed), and the 'f. 178v fourth hand' page is the f. 179 Cipher-3 slip bound upside down.

Split from the former combined target under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): the two Cipher-3 leaves (f. 276, fr. 15571 f. 179; alejandrozarco, PR #25) became matignon1586c3 with their steps and credit; George Lasry's f. 43 credit (a leaf outside this target) removed. Coverage recalculated from measure.json on the Cipher-1 leaves only: 4,325 of 12,994 transcribed tokens (0.333), of ~14,082 with the untranscribed lines (0.307); chance-corrected 0.26 / 0.24. measure.py no longer lists the Cipher-3 leaves.

Contributed (Michael Brackx, issue #64, with Claude Code): ff. 196/201 aligned figure by figure (914 columns, 487 identical) and decoded jointly; f. 201 re-read on the image; names Sainct-Chamarand, la Barge, Montberault, la Binault read on both leaves; q = s (already implied by this folder's own f. 196 head crib), f = h, ss = h, BOX = u and other key corrections; codes 49, 36, 68 proposed.

Contributed (Brackx, issue #68): f. 143r-v decoded with the corrected key, T= = r, f = h, a = a/m, c = p/l; verso ll. 1-7 checked on the image; codes 62 peut, 33 vostre, 40 bien, 54 aussi; 44 = Sire proposed, then withdrawn by him.
Contributed (Brackx, issue #69): f. 173 decoded with the corrected key, 4+ = m/n, 8 = g/e; nine lines checked on the image; codes 15, 27 open, 79 = pour weak.

Contributed (Brackx, issue #70): ff. 155-157 identified as contemporary clear copies of ff. 143r-v, 149v-150 and 154r-v; copies read by eye and aligned with the decodes; codes fixed: 33 vostre, 36 toutesfois, 40 bien, 49 comme, 53 affin, 54 aussi, 62 peut, 76 roi de Navarre, 88 Monsieur du Mayne, 104 mil, hash coustume. f. 154v found to carry two further cipher blocks.

Contributed (Brackx, issue #71): ff. 123-124 decoded with U = u/e/a, d = s/c, q = s/o/a and the copy codes; f. 123v and 124r give connected stretches, f. 123r does not; no clear copy among canvases 128-139.

Review here: canvases 162-164 viewed. f. 155r opens 'S'estant laissé entendre comme il se vouloit départir du Roy de Navarre ...' (the f. 143 cipher, with 49 = comme), 'soubz vostre bon plaisir toutesfois' and 'Et aussi qu'il n'y avoit plus de hasard' legible; f. 155v ends 'Mr du Mayne de ... avril 1586' and begins 'Comme il estoit bien besoing ...' (ff. 149v-150), f. 156r ends 'Mr Forget de ... avril 1586'; f. 157r opens 'En quelle peine nous estions lors pour le payement des deux monstres' and has 'quarante mil escus' (the f. 154 cipher); f. 154v carries two cipher blocks. On canvas 208 the clear phrase 'Le regard dud. siege il s'advance fort' stands inside the f. 201 cipher block, followed by code 36, as #64 says.

Re-measured with measure.py --key key_contrib.json (key.json plus Brackx's letter sets and the copy codes; BOX = u, 44 = Sire and 79 = pour not adopted): 5,480 of 12,994 transcribed tokens read as sense (0.422; 0.389 of ~14,082), up from 4,325 (0.333 / 0.307); scrambled-key control corrected 0.351 / 0.324, up from 0.26 / 0.24. Gains largest on f. 173 (0.28 -> 0.49), f. 201 (0.46 -> 0.62), f. 123v-124v; f. 110 stays at its floor. Part of the gain is the wider letter sets (floors rose 0-2 points).

Brackx (#73): fr. 15571 f. 177r re-transcribed (29 lines) and f. 177v transcribed for the first time (11 lines), in a label set that separates figures the old transcription merged; per-leaf key_f177.json; 84 = le vicomte de Turenne (matches the archivist's summary on the leaf), 24 = mais, 27 = nostre.

Brackx (#77): f. 154v, two cipher blocks (10 + 11 lines) never transcribed, decoded and aligned with the contemporary copy f. 157r: 95.7 / 96.4% letter agreement by his count; δ = c vs ∂ = s, θ = m vs ɟ = s, ꝭ = x, ⊔ = q, 51 = pas, 47 = tous/tout.

Brackx (#78): the f. 18/19 crib completed (ff. 18r 22 lines, 18v 34, 20r 17 against the clear f. 19r-v); ff. 123-124 re-transcribed (156 lines); codes 15 = quoy, 73 = oi, 78 = le roy de Navarre, 82 = le gouverneur de Coul., 84 = le viconte de Turenne, 44 a stop or null (not Sire); code groups split in the old files (4 9 = 49, t 8 = 48, 8 t = 84).

Brackx (#79): f. 110, the leaf recorded as unread, transcribed in full (38 lines; the repo's 54 was a mis-fitted grid) and decoded with the ff. 123-124 key plus H = o/c, w = d/q, + = m/s, long s = p/s, £ = r/f: 78.5% of decoded letters in corpus words by his count (shuffled 35%).

Brackx (#83): ff. 143r-v, 150v, 154r, 173, 196, 201 re-transcribed and f. 150r (32 lines, canvas 157 right) transcribed for the first time; the repo's f150_cipher.txt is the verso; θ = m / ϑ = s, ꝺ̄ = u, ɛ = i; 46 = rien, 61 = beaucoup, 34 = ainsi; copy agreement 87-94% (f. 155r, 155v, 156r, 157r) by his count; misreadings of the copies corrected.

Validated here (brackx_validate.py): his transcriptions and per-leaf keys decoded with this project's beam and 6-gram (not his decoder). Copy agreement f. 154v 0.90/0.94, f. 143r 0.94, f. 143v (covered lines) 0.88, f. 150r 0.84, f. 150v 0.83 (0.91 with his corrected copy), f. 154r 0.90, f. 18r/18v 0.86/0.74 against f. 19; twins ff. 196/201 0.78; set-size-preserving scrambled keys 0.23-0.38 (twins 0.50). Every leaf far above its control; canvases 157 and 116 checked on the image (f. 150r exists, f. 110 has ~38 lines). Target re-measured: 10,303 of 16,677 tokens read as sense (0.618; 0.576 corrected).

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): per-leaf transcriptions and the existing reading_f*.txt / f*_reading.md files; dec.py run with key_contrib.json on every transcribed leaf and saved to texts/<leaf>_decryption.md; f. 154v (never transcribed) linked to the Gallica images of the leaf and its clear copy f. 157r; f. 110 linked to its status note (not read). Missing: the clear copies ff. 155-157 and Michael Brackx's own decodes (issues #64, #68-#71), not in the folder.

One Cipher-1 key from Brackx's eleven per-leaf keys (merge_keys.py): each figure takes the union of the letter sets the leaves give it, each code every value any leaf gives it. Decoded every leaf with it (this project's beam and 6-gram) and scored as brackx_validate.py: the target's 15 documents read 9,855 of 15,705 tokens as sense against 9,609 with the per-leaf keys; every leaf equal or better, copy agreement unchanged within one point (f. 143r 0.93, f. 154r 0.89, f. 154v 0.89/0.93, f. 150r 0.85); scrambled floor 0.121 against 0.100. The per-leaf keys are one key read by different hands, not different keys.

Pruned the union key: dropped any letter a figure took in under 5% of its occurrences across the target (U=a, y=x, B=ss, L=f, ss=h, zb=u). Sense fell from 0.628 to 0.610 (f. 110 0.62 to 0.57), so the union key is kept.

Open code groups 16, 45, 59, 64, me, 101, 102, 103, 9, 44 ranked against the 400 commonest corpus words by the 6-gram score of their contexts in the merged decode (code_lm_test.py). The model prefers two-letter function words everywhere (it would make 59 'es'), so it cannot choose codes from 30-letter contexts.

Code contexts checked against the clear copies: 59 = argent (f. 154r 'nous prester icy de l'[59] a rendre a Paris' = copy f. 157r 'de l'argent à rendre à Paris'; the other contexts, ff. 124r, 154r, 173 twice, fit: 'recouvrer de l'argent soubs ses obligations'); 44 falls at a sentence end both times it meets the f. 156r copy (a stop, as Brackx said); 9 gives 'Comme il' in one copy context and 'Mais s'il' in the other, so it is not one word; 103 (f. 18v) stands where the f. 19 copy itself has an unread word before 'chevaulx légers'. me = mesme and 64 = un fit their contexts ('a eu mesme advis de Bourdeaux', 'avec un peu de forces') but no copy covers them.

Final measure with key_cipher1.json (union key + 59 = argent; final_texts.py): 10,616 of 16,677 tokens read as sense (0.637), set-size-preserving scrambled floor 0.121, corrected 0.587. Per document 0.51 (f. 123r) to 0.77 (f. 201). Full decryptions written per document to texts/.

George Lasry reviewed the page: the decryptions cannot be built into coherent French sentences. Sentence-level check (docs/_check_reading.py, at most one hole in ten words per clean sentence): the nine leaves without a copy give 5-24% clean sentences, the readings from the clear copies 78-88%. texts.label: f. 143r
texts.summary: Mayenne to the King, April 1586, after the capitulation of Castets: its captain, unhappy with the King of Navarre, has agreed to leave him; a treaty of twelve thousand ecus in three months, leave to sell his property and a pardon to be registered by the Parlement. The clear copy is f. 155r.

reading_review.note: the reading follows the contemporary clear copy (Brackx's transcription), read as sentences against the English translation; doubtful words marked (?).
